You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The OpenTelemetry Demo shop itself looks healthy in everything I could observe: all 24 app deployments report available == desired (evidence add81efd-eb38-4d4c-8cee-5312f0d3dffb-t0:b2068bce-de2e-441f-8a06-bbacee696d36), every astronomy-shop pod is Running/Ready with restartCount 0 (79a96f91-d4ed-4f47-a241-1535f5e6b29c-t1:bb8b6fb9-6ca8-4247-b93c-c137c685bf6e), sampled frontend/checkout/recommendation/cart/payment/shipping spans are all HTTP 200 / grpc status 0 (aac308ec-26e2-4f2c-a71d-6adccab18538-t1:6caa57fb-6a91-4a85-9c53-017d9f044ebf), payments and cart work, postgres logs contain no ERROR/FATAL, and every flagd fault-injection flag is still 'off' (1ab15978-b357-4545-83d4-f978be793377-t0:9b3cab4d-eb1f-42e5-9f74-e10852507ba6). The one real, live failure is in the Kafka orders pipeline that was added to this namespace: the orders-validator consumer (group orders-validator, topic orders-fulfillment) hit an unparseable record at offset 20, logged 'record validation failed at offset=20: Expecting value: line 1 column 35 (char 34)' and 'partition processing paused at offset=20', and its code then sleeps forever in a pause loop, so the partition is no longer consumed; its lag grew from 39 (committed_offset 20, end_offset 59 at 23:50:05) to 72 at 23:51:11 while the producer (order-stream, publishing every ~2 s) keeps writing. The topic itself and the broker are healthy (single ISR, no under-replicated or offline partitions), so this is not a Kafka infrastructure fault and not a pod/config change: the consumer Deployment, its ConfigMap and its pod template were created once (23:48:46-23:48:51) and never updated. The trigger is bad data inside the topic; the tooling never exposes message content, the change history integration is not configured, and all telemetry for this environment only starts at ~23:47:48, so I cannot name the producer of the malformed record. I therefore report the malformed record in topic orders-fulfillment as the originating object and the missing error recovery in the orders-pipeline-scripts consumer as a second contributing candidate, with the conclusion partial.

claims.text: The orders-validator pod (orders-validator-6d49bfb98d-nr7lz) started consuming topic=orders-fulfillment group=orders-validator at 23:48:54, processed offsets 0-19 successfully, then logged 'record validation failed at offset=20: Expecting value: line 1 column 35 (char 34)' and 'partition processing paused at offset=20' at 23:48:56 and stopped committing.

Consumer group orders-validator is STABLE but stuck at committed_offset 20 with end_offset 59 (lag 39) on orders-fulfillment partition 0 at 23:50:05; at 23:51:11 the same topic showed total_lag 72, i.e. the backlog kept growing while the group did not advance.

The producing side is still working: order-stream (topic orders-fulfillment, publish interval 2 s) logged 'published order_id=ORD-...' continuously every ~2 s up to and past 23:49:05, so messages keep arriving in the stalled partition.

The orders-validator code mounted from ConfigMap orders-pipeline-scripts (consumer.py) deliberately blocks forever on a validation failure: on exception it logs the error, logs 'partition processing paused', then loops 'while not _shutdown: time.sleep(1)' without skipping, seeking or dead-lettering the record; its Deployment is configured with ORDERS_TOPIC=orders-fulfillment and CONSUMER_GROUP=orders-validator.

The orders pipeline objects were created once and never modified: ConfigMap orders-pipeline-scripts was created 23:48:46 with a single OpenAPI-Generator write and no later update, and the order-stream and orders-validator Deployments each have one ReplicaSet and one pod with restartCount 0, so there is no rollout or template change behind the stall.

Kafka infrastructure is healthy: 1 broker, 4 topics (__consumer_offsets, orders, orders-fulfillment, orders-processed), 53 partitions, 0 under-replicated partitions, 0 offline partitions, no offline brokers, and orders-fulfillment partition 0 has ISR [1] with under_replicated=false.

The other Kafka consumers of the shop are keeping up: group accounting lag 1 on topic orders (committed 18, end 19) and group fraud-detection lag 1 on topic orders (committed 21, end 22), and accounting logged normal 'Order details: {...}' processing without consumer errors after its startup blip.

In the sampled traces of 23:48:56-23:49:06 the shopper path is succeeding: frontend POST /api/checkout, GET /api/recommendations, POST /api/cart and their api-route spans carry http.status_code=200, checkout's oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, PaymentService/Charge, CartService/GetCart, ProductCatalogService/GetProduct and CartService/AddItem spans carry rpc.grpc.status_code=0, and 0 error rows were summarised across all 98 sampled spans.

All 24 OpenTelemetry Demo deployments in astronomy-shop reported available replicas equal to desired replicas at 23:49:07 (delta 0 for accounting, ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, flagd, fraud-detection, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, jaeger, kafka, llm, load-generator, payment, postgresql, product-catalog, product-reviews, quote, recommendation, shipping, valkey-cart, grafana).

No flagd fault-injection feature is active: every flag in ConfigMap flagd-config (demo.flagd.json) has defaultVariant 'off' (productCatalogFailure, cartFailure, adFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad, failedReadinessProbe, emailMemoryLeak, kafkaQueueProblems, llmRateLimitError, llmInaccurateResponse, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu), so the shop-side symptoms are not flag-driven.

The frontend gRPC 'UNAVAILABLE ... connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.40.21:8080' errors (and the matching 10.96.255.208:8080 lines) were considered as the current fault but rejected: they are confined to 23:48:03-23:48:07, immediately after the frontend/backend pods were created at 23:47:48-23:47:50 and before the :8080 backends were listening, and no later error line exists in the window while frontend spans show 200s afterwards.

The record at offset 20 of orders-fulfillment was not written by the currently running order-stream producer: order-stream only publishes ids of the form 'ORD-' + 12 hex characters (e.g. ORD-EF9E3674FB85), whereas the records the validator accepted at offsets 0-19 carried sequential ids ORD-100000..ORD-100019, so an earlier/seeding writer produced the first 21 records and the malformed one; its identity cannot be determined because no tool exposes Kafka message content and the change-history integration is not configured.

A second contributing cause is the consumer's error handling: because orders-pipeline-scripts consumer.py pauses the partition indefinitely on the first unparseable record (no skip, seek, retry limit or dead-letter path), a single bad record converts a data-quality problem into a total halt of the orders-fulfillment -> orders-processed pipeline; this remains a candidate because the script, not the record, is what keeps the lag growing.

Inspect or discard the malformed record at offset 20 of orders-fulfillment (for example reproduce the consumer against the topic to see the payload) and confirm who wrote offsets 0-20; then have the validator skip/dead-letter unparseable records and seek past the poison offset so the group can resume from 20 and drain the backlog, and add lag/validation-failure alerting on topic orders-fulfillment.

gaps: Kafka message content is never exposed by the available tools, so the malformed payload at offset 20 of orders-fulfillment and the identity of the producer that wrote it (and offsets 0-19) could not be determined; the writer is unknown.
The change_history integration is not configured, so any earlier deployment, config or data change during the 24h window (including who seeded topic orders-fulfillment) is unknown rather than absent.

All telemetry in this environment is very young: Prometheus has essentially a single scrape (source_start_at 23:49:07 for the queried series), Jaeger traces only cover 23:48:56-23:49:07, and Loki log points only start ~23:48:44, while the pods were created 23:47:48-23:48:51; therefore the absence of app error signals before ~23:47:48 cannot be assessed and no baseline latency trend could be compared.

No metric series was found for app_payment_transactions_total or http_server_request_duration_seconds_count in the window (queries returned nothing), so per-operation error-rate and latency readings for the shop could not be evaluated from metrics; only sampled traces and logs were available.

The Redis/Valkey read tool returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so valkey-cart server state could not be inspected; the cart path itself looked healthy in traces (valkey-cart spans with grpc/http success on the parent spans).

Whether any consumer of orders-processed exists downstream (and thus any customer-visible fulfillment impact) is unknown: only groups accounting, fraud-detection and orders-validator are registered, and the validator's own commit progress stopped at offset 20.
next_steps: Read the payload at offset 20 of orders-fulfillment with a Kafka client outside these read-only tools and identify which producer wrote offsets 0-20.
Check the deployment/rollout and change history of the orders pipeline setup (job or script that seeded the 21 records) to attribute the malformed record.
After fixing or skipping the record, watch consumer group orders-validator lag on orders-fulfillment to confirm the backlog drains and orders-processed resumes.

content.consumer:
import json
import logging
import os
import signal
import time

from confluent_kafka import Consumer, Producer

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s")
log = logging.getLogger("orders-validator")

BOOTSTRAP = os.environ.get("KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP", "kafka:9092")
TOPIC = os.environ.get("ORDERS_TOPIC", "orders-fulfillment")
OUTPUT_TOPIC = os.environ.get("OUTPUT_TOPIC", "orders-processed")
GROUP = os.environ.get("CONSUMER_GROUP", "orders-validator")

_shutdown = False


def _request_shutdown(signum, frame):
    global _shutdown
    _shutdown = True


def process(value):
    obj = json.loads(value.decode("utf-8"))
    if "order_id" not in obj:
        raise ValueError("record has no 'order_id' field")
    return obj


def main():
    consumer = Consumer(
        {
            "bootstrap.servers": BOOTSTRAP,
            "group.id": GROUP,
            "enable.auto.commit": False,
            "auto.offset.reset": "earliest",
            "max.poll.interval.ms": 86400000,
        }
    )
    out = Producer({"bootstrap.servers": BOOTSTRAP, "enable.idempotence": True})
    consumer.subscribe([TOPIC])
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, _request_shutdown)
    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, _request_shutdown)
    log.info("orders-validator started bootstrap=%s topic=%s group=%s", BOOTSTRAP, TOPIC, GROUP)

    first = True
    while not _shutdown:
        msg = consumer.poll(1.0)
        if msg is None:
            continue
        if msg.error():
            log.warning("consumer error: %s", msg.error())
            continue

        if first:
            log.info("resuming partition at offset=%d", msg.offset())
            first = False

        try:
            order = process(msg.value())
        except Exception as exc:
            log.error("record validation failed at offset=%d: %s", msg.offset(), exc)
            log.error("partition processing paused at offset=%d", msg.offset())
            blocked = 0
            while not _shutdown:
                time.sleep(1)
                blocked += 1
                if blocked % 15 == 0:
                    log.error("partition remains paused at offset=%d", msg.offset())
            break

        result = json.dumps(
            {"source_offset": msg.offset(), "order_id": order["order_id"]},
            separators=(",", ":"),
        )
        out.produce(OUTPUT_TOPIC, value=result.encode("utf-8"))
        out.flush(10)
        consumer.commit(message=msg, asynchronous=False)
        log.info("processed order_id=%s committed_offset=%d", order["order_id"], msg.offset() + 1)

    out.flush(10)
    consumer.close()
    log.info("orders-validator stopped")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
content.producer:
import json
import logging
import os
import time
import uuid

from confluent_kafka import Producer

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s")
log = logging.getLogger("order-stream")

BOOTSTRAP = os.environ.get("KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP", "kafka:9092")
TOPIC = os.environ.get("ORDERS_TOPIC", "orders-fulfillment")
INTERVAL = float(os.environ.get("PRODUCE_INTERVAL_SEC", "2.0"))


def main():
    producer = Producer({"bootstrap.servers": BOOTSTRAP, "enable.idempotence": True})
    while True:
        order_id = "ORD-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:12].upper()
        record = json.dumps({"order_id": order_id, "amount": 1 + int(uuid.uuid4().hex[:2], 16) % 7})
        producer.produce(TOPIC, value=record.encode("utf-8"))
        producer.poll(0)
        producer.flush(10)
        log.info("published order_id=%s", order_id)
        time.sleep(INTERVAL)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
